title: Android 10 BLE + G6 - Stuck in "scanning"
body:
I have a reproduceable problem with XDrip being stuck in Scanning.

1) Reboot the device on Android 10
2) Brain state is stuck in scanning

Solution:
1) Forget device in G5/G6 Status screen
2) Next cycle it sucessfully reconnects and works from that point on... Until I reboot again/or the transmitter fails to connect once because of range etc.

Oneplus 7 Pro on the official Android 10 Version. Newest XDrip Nightly from October 11.

Same here, using a Moto G7 Power which just updated to Android 10. Running nightly build 27 July 2020. It seemed to intermittently connect and disconnect, but overnight I had 2 hr and 4 hr gaps. Failing to reconnect this morning.

Tried the "backup-delete-reinstall" method suggested by tgessendorfer and it looked to work but issues still occurring. 

In desperate need of help here! Wish I had never updated the phone software...

OK so I have at least some success / promising results with another method.

It is a modified version of the "backup - delete - reinstall method"
What I did was:

1. backup settings to SD card 
2. delete Xdrip+
3. clear bluetooth cache by opening Android settings > apps > hamburger menu top right, select show system apps > bluetooth > clear cache
4. reinstall Xdrip+ (I am using latest nightly build, but some of the other comments I have seen mention better results with late Dec 2019 build)
5. BEFORE opening Xdrip > Android Settings > Apps > Xdrip+ > Advanced > Select allow "Modify System Settings" & make sure location access is granted
6. Open Xdrip, do not go through source setup but instead allow restore from backup
7. Make sure all permissions Xdrip requests in notification area are allowed

Not sure if step 3 or 5 was the magic bullet or if they both have to be done, but doing this has allowed me to reconnect to the G5 and get no dropped readings for the last 2.5 hrs. Hopefully this continues... I'll update if something goes wrong, but most promising results I've had since the update threw everything out of whack. Hope this helps someone else.

UPDATE::

After working fine for a few hours the bluetooth connection was lost and refused to connect again of its own accord.

This time I did the same procedure as above but used the Dec 22 2019 version mentioned earlier. I have been running this one for over 12 hours (overnight) with no issue so far. and it is unlikely I would have had no disconnections overnight, so I think it is reconnecting properly. Must be something about how newer versions of Xdrip don't play nice with their bluetooth implementation on Android 10...

UPDATE 2::

Well looks like my hopes were falsely high. Lost connection again today and failed to regain on its own. Back to the drawing board

Mine has been fairly consistent for a week now.  Even after a disconnect because the phone is too far away for too long, it seems to reconnect automatically again.  The things I did, of which some combination seemed to have worked:

1. upgraded to a nightly build (~1.5 weeks ago)
2. allowed location sharing with xdrip per many people's suggestions
3. turned off battery saver mode on my android

It occurred to me that with battery saving mode on, recent versions of android restrict location sharing.  Unfortunately, I don't think there is a way to change the parameters of what battery saving mode does to allow location sharing but to keep doing all its other battery saving things.  Which is disappointing, since I have been running in always-on-battery-saving for ~2 years to get a longer time on battery.

It isn't entirely clear what the cause of this issue is and although the unpairing work-around did seem to help in many cases it now causes problems with the november security patch and results in frequently pop-ups asking for pairing.

As such I have issued a new nightly (15th Nov) which disables the unpairing work-around by default (can be re-enabled with preference option) and introduces a new option `Avoid Scanning` which requires the `Minimize Scanning` feature to be enabled first.

If you have problems with the Android 10 work-around option causing pop-ups but it doesn't work (after a period of time) when you disable this feature, then please try using the `Avoid Scanning` feature to see if that resolves the issue for you.

Because of the fragmentation of the Android Bluetooth stack, in that on some platforms we must scan etc, and some devices have the Android 10 bonding issue and others have the pop-up issue, it is likely that using these preference settings will be the only way to reliably cover all the different combinations. I only have a limited number of handsets to test with this issue so please report back any findings. Thanks.

This was a bug that was addressed with Android 10 workarounds.  After the early November 2020 Android patch, Android 10 workaround resulted in frequent pair requests.  So, we had a new issue triggered by the Android update.  The developer used a different method to address this (and disabled Android 10 workarounds) that did not cause the frequent pair requests.  He released it on November 27, 2020.  Since then, both issues have been addressed.
The frequent pair request issue has been closed (https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/issues/1494).  So will this one.
  
If anyone is experiencing this issue, if you restart your phone and your readings stop, and if you don't have a facebook account, post in the Gitter room.  We will walk you through the steps to fix it.  You can tag me in your post.

If restarting your phone causes the xDrip readings to stop, please install an xDrip release of November 27, 2020 or later.
After that, if you experience connectivity issues, you will need to disable battery optimization of xDrip by Android, enable background location access, and use the recommended xDrip settings.

If you need help, please use the support channels.
https://www.facebook.com/groups/xDripG5
https://gitter.im/jamorham/xDrip-plus
